assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues gave chemistry a new modality: rather than occupying a binding site, a designed small molecule recruits an E3 ligase and removes the target. It reaches proteins long considered undruggable and has changed how researchers and clinicians think about drug action. The design logic (linker, ligase ligand, ternary-complex geometry) is exactly the kind of molecular control over recognition that I value.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the early PROTAC concept with Sakamoto; Ciulli contributed VHL ligand and ternary-complex structural design that made the approach general. The thalidomide-cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito and others) is a related but distinct strand, so a three-person configuration is plausible but leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Multiple degraders are in clinical trials and the field is broadly replicated across academia and industry. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is still pending, so one could argue timing is slightly early, but the chemical principle is well established.
uncertainties: The split of credit between PROTACs and molecular glue degraders (thalidomide mechanism) is unresolved.
I am working from memory on the current clinical status; I have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing turned single-molecule electrical detection into practical long-read DNA and RNA sequencing and a general platform for single-molecule analytical chemistry. It is portable, label-free and widely deployed in clinical and field settings, which speaks directly to my interest in tools that change what people can do. Engineered protein pores and the chemistry of reading modified bases add chemical depth.
assessment.attribution: Branton, Deamer and Kasianowicz proposed and first demonstrated nanopore polynucleotide detection; Bayley engineered protein pores for stochastic sensing; Akeson showed enzyme-controlled DNA translocation that made sequencing feasible. Five credited names exceed three slots, and my selection is a judgement among overlapping founding claims.
assessment.maturity: Commercial sequencers have been in broad use for roughly a decade and the principle is independently validated. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the physical concept (Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz) or the engineered chemistry and enzyme control (Bayley, Akeson) is contested.
Priority among the founding contributors is something I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks by combining a programmable DNA-binding protein with an engineered deaminase. It is a fundamentally chemical idea, direct chemical modification of nucleobases in living cells, and it has opened routes to correcting point mutations and to first clinical applications. The directed-evolution engineering of the deaminases is significant.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work; Komor developed cytosine base editors and Gaudelli developed adenine base editors as lead trainees. Nishida and Kondo independently reported a deaminase-based approach in Japan, so credit could be shared differently. A Liu-centred configuration seems most defensible.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and moving through clinical trials. Long-term safety (off-target deamination) is still being characterised, so maturity is good but not complete.
uncertainties: Whether trainees such as Komor and Gaudelli would be included alongside the principal investigator is uncertain.
The Nishida-Kondo contribution complicates the attribution.
Overlap with CRISPR genome editing already recognised in 2020 and with the prime editing candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs lets chemists install new functional groups into proteins in living cells. This gives precise molecular design control over protein function, biosensors, bioorthogonal handles and therapeutics, and it has spread into biomedicine and biomaterials. It is original and general.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair strategy in E. coli and eukaryotes with Wang; Chin extended it to multiple codons, ribosome engineering and eukaryotic systems. Mehl and Yokoyama made substantive contributions to specific pairs, so the trio is a reasonable but not unique choice.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent use in many laboratories and well-established in practice. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is not clean.
Overlap with directed evolution and the 2018 recognition of evolution methods is limited but worth checking.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that cells organise biochemistry through liquid-liquid phase separation of proteins and nucleic acids reframed cell biology with physical-chemistry concepts, and connects to self-assembly, peptides and condensate materials, which is close to my own area. It has spurred new tools and a drug-discovery interest in condensates.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granules as liquid droplets; Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction framework with reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag contributed theory and sequence grammar. The core claim is relatively clear for the first two names.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing but with active debate about which cellular structures are truly phase-separated and the physiological relevance of in vitro droplets. This is somewhat premature compared with others on my list.
uncertainties: Controversy over rigor of in vivo evidence and terminology.
The topic may sit closer to cell biology or physics than to chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines. Rational lipid design (pKa tuning, microfluidic assembly) turned fragile nucleic acids into drugs reaching billions of people. This is a clear case of a chemical invention changing clinical practice.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues led the foundational lipid chemistry and manufacturing methods; Anderson and Langer developed combinatorial lipid libraries and delivery strategies. Many companies and individuals contributed, and attribution across MacLachlan, Madden and Hope is blurry.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale by COVID-19 vaccines. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised nucleoside modification, so a chemistry prize for delivery is plausible but may be viewed as overlapping.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize.
Many contributors across academia and industry make a clean three-person split difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programming nanoparticle assembly with DNA, and spherical nucleic acids as a distinct class of nanostructure, links nanomaterials with biorecognition. It underlies colorimetric biosensors and intracellular gene regulation agents, which resonates with my work on nanoparticle-based sensing. The programmable-assembly concept is original.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group and Alivisatos's group reported DNA-nanoparticle conjugate assembly in 1996 in parallel; Mirkin developed spherical nucleic acids and applications. Storhoff and Mucic were trainee coauthors. Two-name configuration is reasonable.
assessment.maturity: Concept is well-confirmed with commercial diagnostics and clinical-stage studies, though the clinical impact is more modest than other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the translational impact is large enough relative to others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read out functional enzyme states in complex proteomes, and has driven chemoproteomic discovery of ligandable sites and covalent drugs. It provides chemists and biologists with a powerful way to ask what a molecule does in cells.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt, with Bogyo, Overkleeft and others, shaped the field; Cravatt is the most consistently credited as the principal developer of the broad platform. Solo award would omit important early contributors such as Bogyo and Overkleeft.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and replicated; chemoproteomic fragment screening continues to mature.
uncertainties: Whether attribution should include Bogyo, Overkleeft or Weerapana.
